jobs.title: Physicist-Certified at OKLAHOMA CANCER SPECIALISTS MANAGEMENT COMPA Tulsa, OK
jobs.description:
Physicist-Certified job at OKLAHOMA CANCER SPECIALISTS MANAGEMENT COMPA. Tulsa, OK. Job Description

Job Description

Oklahoma Cancer Specialists and Research Institute (OCSRI) invites you to join a powerful team of cancer experts who invest in the health and well-being of patients through their course of treatment and beyond. The successful candidate will pursue advanced and innovative treatments in a team setting. Such treatments achieve the goal of offering care customized to each patient’s need. OCSRI ensures world class care is close to home as the largest cancer care provider in the Northeastern Oklahoma region. OCSRI’s main campus is located in Tulsa, OK, with 3 satellite clinics in towns surrounding Tulsa.

All OCSRI facilities use CMS Monaco for treatment planning, Mosaiq’s R&V system and Elekta linacs to deliver treatment; each site can sim patients and is attached to a full medical oncology suite. The main campus offers additional treatment options including nuclear medicine, a full imaging suite, an HDR suite and Precision treatment planning for Tomotherapy. 5 linear accelerators are housed at the main campus, including 2 Tomotherapy units, 3 Elekta units (1 Infinity, 2 Versa HD (SRS/SBRT capable)) and a dedicated HDR suite utilizing Flexitron and Oncentra planning.

The successful applicant will join a team consisting of 4 radiation oncologists, 7 dosimetrists, 4 physicists, 1 medical physics assistant and 25 therapists. The department adopts new technology readily and listens to great ideas no matter their origin. If you want to work where your efforts make a difference in how patients receive treatment, OCSRI is the place for you.

Experience with the technology in our clinics, while helpful, is not explicitly required. The team at OCSRI can train any qualified physicist to utilize all software and equipment.

Qualifications: Candidates should possess at least a master’s degree in Physics or Medical Physics from an accredited university and graduated from CAMPEP medical physics residency program. A minimum of 2 years clinical experience (including residency training time), ABR board eligible is required. OCSRI is willing to consider applicants seeking U.S. Residency Sponsorship.

Oklahoma Cancer Specialists and Research Institute is an EEO employer. We offer an excellent Benefits Package which includes medical, dental, vision, 401k, paid time off (PTO) and 9 1/2 holidays per year.

Tulsa is located at green country valley in northeastern Oklahoma, it has distinct weather for all four seasons. The city has grown and expanded significantly in recent years and is truly a great place to raise a family.

Please visit click “Careers at OCSRI” on top, and click “See our job board for open positions” to apply.

jobs.title: Instrumentation and Control Engineer
jobs.description:
One of our companies is looking for an Instrumentation & Controls Specialist

About the Company

Schuermann Analytics is a Tulsa, OK-based systems integration firm specializing in SCADA solutions for municipal water and wastewater plants, designing the control and data infrastructure utilities use to monitor, automate, and remotely manage plant operations. In April 2026, the company was acquired by Scruggs Company, adding SCADA and systems integration capability to Scruggs' municipal water and wastewater platform.

About the Role

We are seeking a skilled and motivated Instrumentation & Controls expert to support the design, implementation, maintenance, and management of industrial control and monitoring systems. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience with PLCs, instrumentation, electrical controls, and project execution, preferably within water and wastewater treatment environments.

Responsibilities
• Design, implement, program, and support PLC-based control systems.
• Program complex control strategies in a variety of different PLC architectures.
• Implement SCADA applications and user interfaces.
• Configure and support field instrumentation.
• Assist with electrical and controls design including:
• Analog and digital signaling systems
• Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs)
• PLC and control panel integration
• Common instrumentation (pressure, flow, level, etc)
• Analytical instrumentation
• Develop and update electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and system documentation.
• Utilize AutoCAD or similar software to create and revise technical drawings and schematics.
• Support water and wastewater treatment systems, including biological and chemical treatment processes.
• Manage projects from initial planning through commissioning and closeout.
• Coordinate with vendors, contractors, operators, and internal teams to ensure successful project execution.
• Perform system testing, startup, calibration, and field troubleshooting.
• Maintain compliance with safety standards, operational procedures, and project requirements.

Qualifications
• Exceptional troubleshooting, problem-solving and analysis skills.
• Strong working knowledge of industrial instrumentation and control systems.
• Experience with electronics and electrical circuits associated with automation and control systems.
• Working knowledge of communication architectures (serial, network, radio, etc).
• Strong organizational and project management skills.
• Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics and technical documentation.
• Experience with PLCs, SCADA systems, or industrial automation platforms.

Preferred Skills
• Experience in water and wastewater treatment processes, including biological and chemical treatment systems.
• Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Automation Technology, or related field.
• Equivalent hands-on experience and technical expertise demonstrated will be strongly considered in place of formal education.
• AutoCAD experience and ability to create technical schematics.

This position may require:
• Working in confined spaces
• Lifting and moving heavy equipment or components
• Climbing ladders and crawling in industrial environments
• Working in hot, cold, wet, or noisy conditions
• Good manual dexterity for handling small components and wiring
• Adequate vision for reading schematics, troubleshooting, and precision work

Work Environment

This role involves a combination of office, shop, and field work at industrial and municipal facilities. Occasional travel and after-hours support may be required depending on project schedules and operational needs.

jobs.title: Processing Lab Technician
jobs.description:
Position Overview

The lab technician is responsible for maintaining processing tanks and the batch treatment area in compliance with applicable policies, procedures, and regulations. The lab tech uses lab equipment to prepare reagents and solutions, troubleshoot lab and test‑related problems, and review test results to ensure standards are met. Typical duties also include measuring levels, pH, and other chemical composition; coordinating and performing chemical adjustments and tank cleaning in accordance with safety procedures, internal work processes, and applicable regulations. This position is classified as safety‑sensitive.

This role is identified as requiring ITAR compliance; qualified candidates must meet the definition of a U.S. Person (per EAR Part 772 and ITAR 120.15):

• An individual who is granted U.S. citizenship

• An individual who is granted U.S. permanent residence (Green Card holder)

• An individual who is granted status as a "protected person"

Essential Functions

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made for qualified individuals with disabilities.

• Maintains processing tanks and batch treatment area per established procedures and regulatory standards; performs "Adds", "Decant", "Builds" and "Drops" of processing tanks as appropriate

• Prepares lab reagents/solutions

• Maintains and operates lab equipment, including pipettes, burettes, TDS, and pH meters; troubleshoots basic lab and test‑related issues; ensures proper use, care, and storage of equipment

• Performs "Adds", "Decant", "Builds" and "Drops" of processing tanks

• Completes accurate, timely, and legible quality records in accordance with AS9100 Quality Policy and NADCAP requirements; inputs QC data into the information management system

• Completes regulatory and hazardous waste reporting and disposal records as required

• Coordinates with internal/external sources for preventative maintenance schedules on all lab equipment

• Reviews customer specifications and identifies applicable data analysis requirements, pass/fail criteria, modulus calculations, test set‑up and configuration

• Maintains quality procedures, quality assurance instructions, and process control procedures to conform to all applicable customer requirements, industry standards, and registration systems; supports and participates as needed in AS/ISO/Nadcap/customer/supplier quality audits of process and products

• Assists in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance quality, productivity, and cost‑effectiveness based on observations and experience; provides technical expertise and works with operators to identify and implement improvements to reduce waste and improve efficiency; implements lean principles, techniques, and methods as appropriate

Work Experience

• Minimum of 1 year experience in a quality role in a manufacturing environment is required

• Previous experience in laboratory operations is required

• Comprehensive understanding of engineering drawings as it relates to the technical aspects of manufacturing and engineering is required; must be able to accurately read and interpret technical drawings and specifications

• Current/Recent HAZOPER and RCCRA certification preferred

Other Required Skills And Abilities

• Must pass a vision color test at pre‑employment and periodically thereafter

• Must be able to pass Hazwoper and RCCRA exams within a reasonable period after hire and must maintain certifications throughout employment in role

• Understanding manufacturing, material flow, process change, and quality processes is preferred

• Experience in continuous improvement concepts such as Six Sigma and Lean is preferred

• Knowledge of and experience with the requirements of AS9100

• Knowledge in RCCA (Root Cause Corrective Action) Analysis

Physical Demands and Work Environment

• Regularly stand and walk throughout the facility, stand for long

jobs.title: Electrical & Instrumentation Journeyman (Oil & Gas Manufacturing)
jobs.description:
Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced Electrical & Instrumentation Journeyman Level II to support the build, wiring, testing, and commissioning of oil & gas measurement equipment, including meter tubes, ultrasonic meter runs, orifice systems, sample systems, and packaged measurement skids. This role is ideal for a technician with strong electrical fundamentals and hands-on instrumentation experience who can work independently in a manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities
• Install, wire, and terminate electrical and instrumentation components for:
• * Ultrasonic, turbine, and orifice meter systems
• Flow computers, transmitters, and RTDs
• Sample systems, analyzers, and probe assemblies
• Control panels, junction boxes, and skid-mounted I&E systems
• Perform conduit routing, cable tray installation, cable pulls, and panel terminations according to shop standards.
• Read and interpret electrical schematics, loop sheets, wiring diagrams, P&IDs, and measurement drawings.
• Assist in the build and testing of measurement skids, including powering up systems, verifying signals, and supporting FAT procedures.
• Troubleshoot electrical and instrumentation issues using multimeters, loop calibrators, and diagnostic tools.
• Support measurement PM’s and drafting teams with redlines, revisions, and technical feedback.
• Document work performed, materials used, and test results for QA and traceability.

Required Qualifications
• Valid Journeyman Electrician License (state-issued).
• 2–3 years of electrical experience.
• Working knowledge of instrumentation, including transmitters, flow computers, RTDs, solenoids, and control wiring.
• Ability to read and interpret P&IDs, loop sheets, wiring diagrams, and measurement schematics.
• Proficiency with hand tools, power tools, and electrical test equipment.
• Ability to lift 50+ lbs, work in fabrication environments, and perform physically demanding tasks.
• Strong attention to detail and commitment to measurement accuracy.

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience working in fabrication, skid manufacturing, or with oil & gas equipment.
• Experience wiring PLC/VFD panels, motor controls, and low-voltage control systems.
• Knowledge of hazardous area classifications and wiring methods (Class I Div 1/2).
• Experience supporting FAT testing, signal verification, and commissioning.

jobs.title: Associate Electronic and Optical Materials Device Fabrication Engineer
jobs.description:
Description

Are you motivated to develop next-generation optical and optoelectronic devices that protect our nation and advance scientific discovery?

Do you thrive in a cleanroom setting, working with expert teams to build high precision, multilayer optics and develop groundbreaking electronic materials?

If so, we're looking for someone like you to join our team at APL.

We are seeking a Junior Electronic and Optical Materials Device Fabrication Engineer to help us fabricate world-class micro- and nanoscale devices. The role is predominantly fabrication-focused, with a vast majority of working hours spent in a cleanroom or laboratory environment, including the cleanroom at JHU-APL in Laurel, MD and other multi-user facilities within a 20 min to 1 hr drive. You will be joining a hardworking team of engineers and scientists who are passionate about developing ground-breaking solutions to solve the nation's critical challenges!

In this role, you'll...
• Design and optimize multilayer layouts with Python scripting for layout generation and data analysis.
• Develop advanced fabrication recipes for multilayer optics using e-beam lithography and direct-write lithography on various optical substrates.
• Apply AI and machine-learning approaches to improve fabrication processes
• Maintain version-controlled GDS/layout databases with Python-based automation for parametric layout generation, fracturing, and design rule checking, and develop data-analysis pipelines linking design, fabrication, and metrology data for CD, overlay, and yield trends.
• Refine deposition techniques across systems such as e-beam, thermal, and sputter evaporators, PECVD, ALD, and MOCVD to enhance device quality.
• Characterize thin films and processes using tools like SEM/EDS, XPS, XRD, AFM, ellipsometry, and film stress analysis to ensure quality and performance.
• Execute precision etching processes to meet tight design specifications and tolerances.
• Maintain and update process documentation, including runsheets, for accuracy and repeatability.

The Scientific Programmer II bridges the gap between scientific development and operational production by integrating, testing, validating, and supporting scientific software applications in a remote work environment. • Demo code and production rules at delivery, and provide ongoing guidance and support during transition to facilitate successful adoption and operational handoff.

• Participate in code reviews across projects to promote code quality, maintainability, adherence to standards, and knowledge sharing among team members.
